market_context.summary: Saudi online spending keeps setting records: e-commerce payments on mada cards alone reached SAR 30.7 billion in October 2025, up 68% year on year, according to the Saudi Central Bank bulletin (credit cards excluded). By web audience in October 2026, amazon.sa and noon.com lead, followed by SHEIN, Temu and AliExpress, while the store-building platform Salla, whose own site draws about 5 million visits, points to a sizeable independent-store segment. In beauty and personal care the pharmacy chains are the online category leaders: Similarweb ranks nahdionline.com and al-dawaa.com first and second among beauty sites, Nahdi reports 30.6% of revenue from online channels, and ECDB models a 15-20% online share with Nahdi, Nice One and Trendyol as the top three retailers. Grocery e-commerce (Panda, Danube, Lulu, Carrefour) and quick-commerce apps (Ninja, HungerStation, Nana, Keeta) are active but disclose little. No regulator-verified platform market shares were found.

key_facts.fact: E-commerce sales through mada cards reached a record SAR 30.7 billion in October 2025 (+68% year on year from SAR 18.3 billion) and SAR 88.3 billion in Q3 2025; the figures exclude credit-card payments. Latest official figure found; about 13 months old.

ranking_method_note: Scores (1-5) were assigned by the researcher from evidence retrieved on 2026-11-26 and applied to the fixed rubric: weighted_score = 0.20*ecommerce_significance + 0.25*beauty_category_relevance + 0.20*consumer_reach + 0.15*brand_competitor_coverage + 0.20*data_integration_feasibility, rounded to 2 decimals; priority_rank = rank by weighted_score within the country; ties broken by beauty_category_relevance, then consumer_reach as specified. Where a tie survived both rubric tie-breaks, three further deterministic tie-breaks were added by the researcher (not part of the brief): higher ecommerce_significance, then the higher in-country monthly web-visit estimate (Semrush, October 2026, as cited in each record), then alphabetical order. Scoring anchors used consistently across the three countries: consumer_reach 5 = >=10M estimated in-country monthly web visits or an equivalent survey-evidenced scale, 4 = 2-10M (or >=1M company-reported active app users), 3 = 0.5-2M, 2 = 100-500K, 1 = <100K or no credible number; brand_competitor_coverage 5 = >=8 of the 12 reference mass-market brands verified as listed, 4 = 5-7 verified or brand-owner official stores verified, 3 = 2-4 verified or a full-range retailer whose assortment could not be verified (neutral), 2 = mass brands largely absent / unverified limited-range or unbranded platform, 1 = verified absent; data_integration_feasibility 5 = documented official API exposing catalogue and competitive price/offer data, 4 = open developer portal with a documented seller API on a platform where brand owners run their own stores (own-shop data only) or public storefront data readable without login, 3 = public pages retrievable without an API, or a seller API whose reference was not verified or that only helps a brand that sells on that platform, 2 = automated access refused or app/location-gated with no usable API, 1 = app-only. The beauty_relevance and data_collection_feasibility labels follow the scores (4-5 high, 3 medium, 1-2 low). Web-visit estimates understate app-first platforms; no regulator-verified or audited market-share figure was found for any platform, so every reach figure is a third-party estimate, a survey result or company-reported. Scores are judgements, not measurements. In this file one tie survived both rubric tie-breaks: SHEIN and Temu (both 2.80, beauty relevance 2, reach 4, significance 4); SHEIN is ranked higher on the Semrush estimate of Saudi visits (7.97M against 5.61M). Ninja ranks above Trendyol (both 2.85) through the rubric's own reach tie-break.

platforms.priority_rationale: Largest measured online audience in the Kingdom plus the only documented API returning competitive price data. platforms.confidence_note: Reach and API evidence are strong, although the two traffic estimators disagree by a factor of more than three; brand coverage is only partly verified.
